beats.care: A stronger rupee eases costs of imported things like phones, fuel and foreign fees. But RBI can't spend its reserves forever.
beats.what: The rupee closed at 94.89 per dollar on Friday, its sixth straight gain and over 2% stronger than its record low on 8 October.
beats.why: RBI cut dollar demand from oil companies and limited betting against the rupee, and has sold dollars to steady it.

cards.note: 25 Sep figure worked out from the reported $12.95B fall.
cards.title: India's forex reserves (billion dollars)

cards.body: Since its special measures began on 8 June, RBI has reportedly used about $75 to 80 billion through dollar sales and swaps. In the latest week, gold holdings also fell $1.3 billion as prices moved.
Reserves are like an emergency fund for the country. RBI uses them to pay for imports in a crisis and to stop the rupee falling too fast.
cards.title: why does RBI keep reserves?

cards.body: Even after two weeks of falls, reserves are still about $35 billion higher than at the end of March 2026.

opts: RBI sold dollars to support the rupee
cards.q: Why did India's forex reserves fall while the rupee rose?
cards.why: Selling dollars from reserves adds supply in the market, which props up the rupee but shrinks the stash.

hook: The rupee is *winning again*. So why is RBI's dollar pile shrinking?

learn.t: Forex reserves are RBI's stash of dollars and gold. They fell $21.5 billion in two weeks, to $726 billion.
